screening_decisions.reason: This is a general review article about complications of enteral nutrition. It does not report a randomised controlled trial comparing PEG versus NGT. No specific comparison between feeding methods is made.
This is a review article describing techniques and indications for enteral feeding. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing PEG versus NGT.
This is a systematic review, not a primary randomised controlled trial. While it reviews RCTs comparing PEG and NGT, it is itself a secondary study.
This is a retrospective study comparing timing of enteral nutrition initiation (within 24h vs 24-72h), not comparing PEG versus NGT. The study design does not meet the RCT requirement.
This is an opinion/critical review article discussing the evidence for PEG use. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing PEG versus NGT.
This study compares percutaneous radiological gastrostomy (PRG) versus PEG, not PEG versus NGT. The intervention comparison does not match the review question.
This is an RCT but it compares quality of life assessment instruments (EuroQol vs SF-36), not PEG versus NGT feeding methods.
This is an observational cross-sectional study examining associations between oral health, dysphagia, and malnutrition. It is not an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT.

This is a multicentre RCT that includes a comparison of PEG versus nasogastric feeding in dysphagic stroke patients (321 patients enrolled). The population (stroke patients with dysphagia) and intervention comparison (PEG vs NGT) match the selection criteria. Outcomes include death and poor outcome at 6 months.
This is a prospective observational study assessing PEG safety in 119 patients. There is no comparison group (NGT) and it is not a randomised controlled trial.
This is a review article about vitamin D content in enteral nutrition formulas. It is not an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT.
This is a retrospective study comparing two PEG insertion techniques (pull-through vs push), not PEG versus NGT. The comparison does not match the review question.
This is a validation study of a dysphagia screening questionnaire. It is not an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT feeding methods.

This is a prospective audit comparing nasal loop (a technique to secure NGT) versus PEG. While it involves NGT, the comparison is not standard NGT versus PEG, and it is not a randomised controlled trial.
This is a quality improvement study describing changes to PEG service delivery. It is not an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT.

This is an RCT but it compares management of residual volumes (RV >400mL vs RV >200mL) in patients receiving enteral feeding via NGT or PEG. The primary comparison is not PEG versus NGT, but rather residual volume management strategies.

This is a case series of 10 patients with anorexia nervosa receiving enteral feeding. It is not an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT, and the population (anorexia nervosa) does not match the swallowing disturbance/dysphagia criteria.
This study compares PEG versus Stamm gastrostomy (surgical gastrostomy), not PEG versus NGT. The comparison does not match the review question.

This is a prospective randomised trial comparing NGT versus PEG (90 patients: 46 NGT, 44 PEG). The study reports outcomes including aspiration, complications, feeding interruption, and patient/nursing satisfaction. This matches the selection criteria for RCTs comparing PEG vs NGT.

This is an RCT comparing PEG versus NGT in 40 patients with neurological dysphagia. The primary outcome includes treatment failure (blocked or displaced tubes, refusal to continue treatment), which directly matches the review's primary outcome of intervention failure. This study clearly meets all selection criteria.
Cross-sectional observational study on anemia prevalence. Not an RCT, does not compare PEG vs NGT feeding.
Literature review and case report, not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
Meta-analysis comparing radiologic gastrostomy, PEG, and surgical gastrostomy - not PEG vs NGT.
Selective literature review on malnutrition, not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
Cochrane systematic review, not a primary RCT.
Nonrandomized retrospective study comparing PEG techniques, not PEG vs NGT.
Observational study on dysphagia incidence, not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
Case report, not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
Observational study on nutrition therapy impact, not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
Prospective observational study comparing NG vs oral feeding, not PEG vs NGT.
Observational study on videofluoroscopic findings, not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
Review article on enteral feeding methods, not an RCT.
Randomised prospective trial comparing PEG vs NGT in adults with acute dysphagic stroke. Reports treatment failure (50% NG vs 0% PEG). Meets all criteria.
Randomised trial comparing PEG vs NGT in head and neck cancer patients with swallowing disturbances from treatment. Reports complications relevant to intervention failure.
RCT comparing PEG vs surgical gastrostomy, not PEG vs NGT.
Review article on tube feeding techniques, not an RCT.
Randomised prospective study comparing PEG vs NGT in adults with acute dysphagic stroke. Reports treatment failure (0/16 gastrostomy vs 3/14 nasogastric). Meets all criteria.
Review on children with intestinal failure. Wrong population (children), not an RCT, wrong comparison.
Study developing a dysphagia scale, not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
Cochane systematic review that found no RCTs. The review itself is not an eligible primary study.
This is not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT. It is a review/article about hospital malnutrition prevalence and nutrition screening recommendations. Does not meet any of the key inclusion criteria.
This is explicitly stated as a 'PURPOSE OF REVIEW' article discussing enteral feeding techniques. It is not a randomised controlled trial comparing PEG vs NGT.
While this is an RCT, it compares endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) versus operative gastrostomy (OG/surgical), not PEG versus nasogastric tube (NGT). The comparison does not match the protocol.
This is a clinical practice guideline from ESPEN, not a randomised controlled trial. Guidelines synthesize evidence but are not primary research studies.
This is a review article aimed at primary care physicians discussing diagnosis and management strategies. It is not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is a retrospective review comparing three gastrostomy techniques (FPG, PEG, SEG), not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT. No nasogastric tubes are included in the comparison.

This is a Cochrane systematic review that specifically includes RCTs comparing PEG vs NGT feeding in dysphagic stroke patients. The abstract states: 'Route of feeding: percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) and nasogastric tube (NGT) feeding did not differ for case fatality...but PEG was associated with fewer treatment failures'. This directly addresses the PICO question and reports intervention failure outcomes. As a systematic review including relevant RCTs, it should be included for potential data extraction.

While this study compares PEG vs NGT in older adults with indications for enteral feeding, it is explicitly described as a 'prospective, multicenter cohort study', not a randomised controlled trial. The authors even state 'A randomized controlled study is needed'.
This is a retrospective study comparing patients with PEG vs those without PEG (who received oral feeding only). It does not compare PEG vs NGT, and is not an RCT.
This is a population-based registry study assessing survival after various interventions in ALS patients. It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.
This is a methodological paper describing reporting standards for RCTs. It is not a clinical trial comparing PEG vs NGT.
This study evaluates organoleptic characteristics of oral nutritional supplements (SON). It does not involve PEG or NGT tubes and is not an RCT.
This meta-analysis compares gastric vs post-pyloric feeding routes in critically ill patients. It does not compare PEG vs NGT tubes.
This is a cross-sectional study examining associations between nutritional parameters and hospital length of stay. It does not compare PEG vs NGT and is not an RCT.
This appears to be a general review article about enteral nutrition principles and practices. It is not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
This is a review article about PEG indications, technique, and nursing care. It is not an RCT comparing PEG vs NGT.
This systematic review compares gastric vs post-pyloric feeding routes in ICU patients. It does not compare PEG vs NGT tubes.
This is a case report about a novel cause of dysphagia (PVC-associated). It does not involve PEG or NGT feeding and is not an RCT.

While this study compares PEG vs NGT in head and neck cancer patients with dysphagia, it is explicitly described as a 'retrospective review'. The authors state 'A randomized prospective trial is needed'. Not an RCT.
This is a descriptive analytic study of PEG tube placement outcomes and patient/caregiver perspectives. It is a single-arm study of PEG patients only, with no comparison to NGT. Not an RCT.

This RCT compares two methods of securing nasogastric tubes (looped NGT vs conventional adhesive dressing), not PEG versus NGT. While the population (stroke patients with dysphagia) matches the review criteria, the intervention comparison does not address the research question of PEG vs NGT feeding.

This RCT compares two different enteral nutrition formulas (whey protein vs casein) delivered via nasogastric tube. Both groups received NGT feeding; there is no comparison between PEG and NGT. The study focuses on inflammatory markers rather than intervention failure outcomes.

While this RCT compares PEG versus non-PEG (NGT) feeding, the population consists of mechanically-ventilated patients with ventilator-associated pneumonia and gastroesophageal reflux, not adults with swallowing disturbances or dysphagia. The primary outcome was gastroesophageal reflux reduction, not intervention failure related to tube feeding.

This is a retrospective observational study, not a randomised controlled trial. It examines associations between nutritional status and clinical outcomes without any intervention comparison. There is no comparison of PEG versus NGT feeding methods.

This study uses a quasi-experimental design (not an RCT) comparing usual care versus an aspiration risk-reduction protocol. The intervention involves head-of-bed elevation and small-bowel feeding placement, not a comparison between PEG and NGT feeding methods.

This is a descriptive report of a new PEG technique, not a randomised controlled trial. It reports outcomes in 12 children and 19 adults without a comparison group. There is no comparison between PEG and NGT feeding, and the inclusion of pediatric patients falls outside the adult-only scope of the review.
